text: I’ll interpret this as a top-milled, constant-depth serpentine groove: three 4 mm straight passes along the 60 mm direction, on 7 mm pitch so the straight-pass webs are exactly 3 mm. The two U-turns stay inside the plate; the inlet is the first pass at the left edge and the outlet is the third pass at the right edge. The 5 mm groove runs from the top face down to 3 mm above the plate bottom. For meshing, I’ll first make and inspect the exact CAD solids, then use the extracted water volume as the only mesh region.

The first preview exposed a construction error before meshing: the straight passages are present, but the turn solids were transformed incorrectly, leaving a detached lump and invalid volume conservation. I’ll inspect the installed placement and primitive conventions, then rebuild only after correcting that.

The issue is confirmed: this installed build123d centers `Box` on all axes by default, while the intended coordinates treated boxes as minimum-corner anchored. I’ll now make every alignment explicit; cylinders remain centered in plan but start at the groove floor in Z.

The corrected water volume is one connected solid, conserves the block volume exactly, and the preview shows the intended three-pass path. Next I’ll inspect the resulting face topology so the two end faces can be named from their construction geometry (planar X-normal faces at the known pass ends), not guessed from the overall bounding box.

The topology has exactly two 20 mm² planar end faces at the constructed pass endpoints: inlet at `(0, 13, 5.5) mm` with outward normal `−X`, and outlet at `(60, 27, 5.5) mm` with outward normal `+X`. I’ll bind those faces by these known construction properties, assign every other water face to `walls`, and export both CAD solids plus the watertight, jointly tessellated patch set.

The exported patch union is closed and consistently wound (876 triangles, zero open/flipped/non-manifold edges). I’ll use a 1 mm Cartesian background grid with one surface-refinement level, giving roughly 0.5 mm cells at the channel boundary—about eight cells across the 4 mm width and ten through the 5 mm depth. First I’ll create and verify the coarse background mesh, then snap it to the water surface.

The 9,548-cell background mesh has the intended uniform 1 mm spacing and encloses the channel. I’ll now retain the connected region containing a point in the first straight pass, refine all three named surfaces once, and snap without boundary layers.

Snappy stopped before modifying the mesh because OpenFOAM 2512 reads numerical-scheme subdictionaries even for meshing; my placeholder `fvSchemes` was too sparse. I’ll add the standard required scheme entries, rewrite the snappy dictionary in this accepted step, and rerun from the unchanged background mesh.

Castellation succeeded to 21,382 retained water cells, but snapping stopped because the shipped quality include lacks the `errorReduction` entry expected by this executable. Since `-overwrite` had already written the intermediate castellated mesh, I’ll inspect the installed quality dictionary before restarting cleanly from `blockMesh`.

The correct OpenFOAM 2512 quality template is `caseDicts/mesh/generation/meshQualityDict.cfg`. I’ll use that version-specific include, regenerate the background mesh, and rerun the complete castellate-and-snap process.

The final snapped mesh completed with 21,382 cells and no quality faces rejected during meshing. I’ll now run the binding `checkMesh` test and inspect patch sizes and mesh bounds before visualizing the water mesh.

`checkMesh` passes: one connected region, three correct patches, 21,382 cells, maximum non-orthogonality 54.8°, skewness 0.464, and mesh volume `3.55926×10⁻⁶ m³` versus CAD water volume `3.559823×10⁻⁶ m³` (about 0.016% difference). I’ll render the final volume mesh and separately highlight inlet/outlet patches to visually confirm connectivity and naming.

The mesh itself is complete; only the visualization utility option differs in this OpenFOAM build (`-noFields` is unsupported). I’ll query its installed command-line options and then export the mesh using the supported form.
The supported spelling is `-no-fields`. I’ll use that and render a clipped isometric view so both the serpentine shape and the internal cell distribution are visible.

The final rendering confirms a continuous three-pass water mesh with resolved U-turns and two distinct open end sections. I did not run a flow/thermal solve or set boundary conditions; the work is limited to CAD, named surfaces, and the water-side mesh as requested.

The completion checks found one metadata omission, not a mesh defect: the snappy dictionary contains the correct interior point `(10, 13, 5.5) mm`, but the surface manifest did not record it. I’ll inspect `export_patches`’ installed argument name and re-export the identical surfaces with that point embedded for independent validation.

The exporter accepts `location_in_mesh`. I’ll regenerate the same tessellation and manifest with the already-used interior point, then redeclare completion; this does not alter the existing volume mesh.
All exported geometry metadata now matches the meshing setup: the surface is closed, the seed is inside the first pass, and the existing mesh still has the passing `checkMesh` result.
